cohort: The study included infants less than 3 months of age (EOS <7 days, CA-LOS 7-90 days) presenting with sepsis at the sole medical center in southern-Israel between 2007 and 2013.
finding: Early-onset sepsis was characterized by higher rates of perinatal risk factors, Streptococcus agalactiae infections, normal temperature, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and mortality, while fever and Streptococcus pneumoniae infections were more common in community-acquired late-onset sepsis.
mod_finding: Non-vaginal delivery was identified as a risk factor for early-onset sepsis.
birth_weight: Low birth-weight was identified as a risk factor for EOS.
gest_age: Prematurity was a significant characteristic of both groups, more common in EOS (42.9% vs. 17.0%).
